tour.title: Window tour
tour.blurb: A quick look around the window.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text: This short tour shows where things are. Click Next to go on, or Close at any time.

steps.title: Design tab
steps.text: The Design tab holds the tools for drawing, editing and modeling. The tabs under it hold Sheets, Layers, Components and Clipart.

steps.title: Tools
steps.text: Tools sit in groups. Hover over a tool to see what it does, and click it to open its form here. The ? at the top of a form opens its help.

steps.title: The view
steps.text: Draw and pick things here. Scroll to zoom, and drag with the middle or right button (or hold Space) to pan. Press F to see the whole job.

steps.title: 2D and 3D views
steps.text: Switch between the flat drawing and the 3D view with these tabs, or with F2 and F3. In 3D, drag to turn the view.

steps.title: Assembly View
steps.text: After you preview toolpaths, the Assembly View puts the cut parts together so you can check how they fit.

steps.title: Toolpaths panel
steps.text: Everything about cutting lives here: the material, the toolpaths, the preview and saving the file for your machine.

steps.title: Help is always close
steps.text: Each panel title and each form has a ? button. Help > Zeroed Help (F1) has every tool, and Help > Tutorial Browser brings this guide back.

machine.title: Set up your machine
machine.blurb: Machine, post processor and bits. Do this first.

steps.title: What you will set
steps.text: Machine Configuration holds your machine's details. These cards say what to set. Read them first, because the dialog covers this card until you click OK.

steps.title: Its size and units
steps.text: You will name your machine, pick the units your controller uses and type the X, Y and Z travel under Working Area.

steps.title: Its post processor
steps.text: Under Add post processor, choose your controller and click Add. The post processor writes the file your machine reads, so it has to match.

steps.title: A rotary axis, if you have one
steps.text: Under Rotary Axis, set the axis letter, whether it reads degrees or linear units, and its direction. Add a rotary post processor too.

steps.title: Open it now
steps.text: Open the Machine menu and pick Machine Configuration. Set these things and click OK. This card comes back when you do, then click Next.

steps.title: Your bits
steps.text: Click Tool Database and enter the real diameter, flute length, shank and holder of each bit, with feeds and speeds you trust. The preview uses them to find collisions.

steps.title: Before your first cut
steps.text: Open Help Contents from the Help menu and read Before You Cut. Run the first file in the air with your hand on the stop button.

cutout.title: Cut out a part
cutout.blurb: Cut a shape free, held in place with tabs.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed the size and thickness of your material.

steps.title: Material size
steps.text: Type the width, height and thickness of your material, then click OK.

steps.title: Bring in a shape
steps.text: Click Import Bitmap / Vectors to open an SVG, DXF, DWG, EPS, AI or PDF file. No file yet? Use Draw Rectangle instead.

steps.title: Pick the shape
steps.text: Click the outline of the part in the view.

steps.title: Cut it out
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click 2D Profile Toolpath.

steps.title: Choose the bit and depth
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick an end mill. Set the cut depth to the material thickness and Machine Vectors to Outside / Right.

steps.title: Hold it with tabs
steps.text: Turn on Add tabs to toolpath so the part stays put until the end of the cut, then click Calculate.

steps.title: Inside cuts come first
steps.text: Add any pockets and holes the same way. Toolpaths run from the top of this list down, so keep the outline last.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to watch the cut before you make it.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths, pick your machine's post processor and save the file.

sign.title: V-grooved sign
sign.blurb: Text carved with a V-bit inside a border.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed the size and thickness of your board.

steps.title: Board size
steps.text: Type the width, height and thickness of the board, then click OK.

steps.title: Draw a border
steps.text: Click Draw Rectangle to draw the edge of the sign.

steps.title: Place the rectangle
steps.text: Drag in the view to draw it, or type its size and click Create. Click Close when it looks right.

steps.title: Add the words
steps.text: Click Create Text to write the words of the sign.

steps.title: Type the text
steps.text: Click in the view where the text goes, then type the words and pick a font and a height. Click Close when done.

steps.title: Pick what to carve
steps.text: Click the text in the view. Hold Shift and click the border to pick it too.

steps.title: V-Groove
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click V-Groove / Engraving Toolpath.

steps.title: Choose the bit
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick a V-bit. Keep the other settings and click Calculate.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to see the carving in 3D before you cut.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths, pick your machine's post processor and save the file. Read Before You Cut in the help before the first run.

relief.title: Relief
relief.blurb: A raised 3D shape, roughed and finished.

steps.title: Draw the outline
steps.text: Click Draw Ellipse. The relief grows from this outline.

steps.title: Place the ellipse
steps.text: Drag in the view to draw an oval, then click Close.

steps.title: Pick the outline
steps.text: Click the oval in the view so it shows as picked.

steps.title: Make a shape
steps.text: Click Create Round Shape to raise a rounded dome from the outline.

steps.title: Shape and height
steps.text: Set the Profile Angle (lower is flatter), tick Limit or Scale to set the height, and click Apply. Click Close when you like it.

steps.title: Look at it in 3D
steps.text: Click 3D View to see the relief. Drag to turn it.

steps.title: Rough it out
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click 3D Roughing Toolpath. It clears most of the wood with a bigger bit.

steps.title: Roughing bit
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick a big end mill, then click Calculate.

steps.title: Finish it
steps.text: Click 3D Finishing Toolpath. A small ball nose bit leaves the smooth surface.

steps.title: Finishing bit
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick a ball nose bit, then click Calculate.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to watch both passes carve the relief.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths and save one file per bit if your machine has no tool changer.

rotary.title: Rotary
rotary.blurb: Wrap a design round a turning blank.

steps.title: Set up the blank
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed about the blank on your rotary axis.

steps.title: Make it a rotary job
steps.text: Under Job Type, pick Rotary. Set the Blank Shape, Blank Length and Blank Diameter. Set Blank Along to the axis your rotary spindle is mounted on. Then click OK.

steps.title: Your design is flat
steps.text: The view now shows the blank unrolled: its length one way and the distance round it the other. Draw flat here and it wraps when you cut.

steps.title: Add a design
steps.text: Click Create Text to write something to carve round the blank.

steps.title: Type the text
steps.text: Click in the view where the text goes, then type the words and pick a font and a height. Click Close when done.

steps.title: Pick what to carve
steps.text: Click the text in the view.

steps.title: Clear it with a raster
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click Pocket Toolpath. On a rotary job it always clears with a raster along the blank, with the rotary axis turning between passes.

steps.title: Choose the bit
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick an end mill. Set the cut depth and click Calculate.

steps.title: Watch it turn
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths, turn on Animate preview and click Preview All Toolpaths. The blank turns under the bit, as it will on your machine.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths and pick a rotary post processor, which writes the moves round the blank. Run a scrap cut first: if it reads mirrored, flip Direction in Machine Configuration.

trace.title: Trace a picture
trace.blurb: Turn an image into vectors you can cut.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed the size and thickness of your material.

steps.title: Material size
steps.text: Type the width, height and thickness of your material, then click OK.

steps.title: Bring in the picture
steps.text: Click Import Bitmap / Vectors and open your image. Black and white pictures with clean edges trace best.

steps.title: Pick the picture
steps.text: Click the picture in the view.

steps.title: Trace it
steps.text: Click Trace Bitmap.

steps.title: Fit the lines
steps.text: Set the Threshold, Noise Filter and Corner Fit. Click Preview to check the lines, then click Apply.

steps.title: Pick the new vectors
steps.text: Click Close, then click the vectors you want to cut. They lie exactly over the picture.

steps.title: Cut along them
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click 2D Profile Toolpath.

steps.title: Choose the bit
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick a bit. Set the cut depth and click Calculate.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to see the cut before you make it.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths, pick your machine's post processor and save the file.

twoSided.title: Two-sided job
twoSided.blurb: Cut both faces, flipping the board between.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed the size and thickness of your material.

steps.title: Make it double sided
steps.text: Under Job Type, pick Double Sided. Under Flip Direction, say how you will turn the board over. Then click OK.

steps.title: Top side first
steps.text: Press 1 to work on the top side. Draw or import what goes on this face.

steps.title: Cut the top
steps.text: Pick a vector and click 2D Profile Toolpath, or any other toolpath. Choose the bit and click Calculate.

steps.title: Now the bottom
steps.text: Press 2 to work on the bottom side. Draw what goes on this face and add its toolpaths the same way.

steps.title: Preview both sides
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths, then Preview All Sides to see both faces cut in order.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths and save a file for each side. Run the top file, turn the board over the way you set in Job Setup, then run the bottom file.

nesting.title: Nest parts on a sheet
nesting.blurb: Pack parts to use as little material as possible.

steps.title: Set up the sheet
steps.text: Click Job Setup and enter your sheet size and thickness. A full sheet is 96 x 48 in.

steps.title: Sheet size
steps.text: Type the width, height and thickness of your sheet, then click OK.

steps.title: Bring in your parts
steps.text: Click Import Bitmap / Vectors to open your parts, or draw them on the Design tab.

steps.title: Pick the parts
steps.text: Drag a box around the parts in the view to pick them all.

steps.title: Nest them
steps.text: Click Nest Parts.

steps.title: Leave room for the bit
steps.text: Type the Tool Dia. and the Clearance between parts, then click Apply. Zeroed adds more sheets when the parts need them.

steps.title: See your sheets
steps.text: The Sheets tab lists each sheet. Click one to work on it.

steps.title: Cut them out
steps.text: Pick the parts on a sheet and click 2D Profile Toolpath.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths, pick your post processor and save a file for each sheet.

box.title: Box with joints
box.blurb: Panels joined, then checked in the Assembly View.

steps.title: Draw the panels
steps.text: Click Draw Rectangle. Each side of the box is one rectangle.

steps.title: One rectangle per side
steps.text: Draw four sides and a bottom with a gap between them. Sides that meet must have edges of the same length. Click Close when done.

steps.title: Pick all the panels
steps.text: Press Cmd+A, or drag a box around the panels, to pick them all.

steps.title: Joint Creator
steps.text: Click Joint Creator. It cuts the joints into the edges for you.

steps.title: Box from Selection
steps.text: Click Box from Selection. Finger joints are picked. Tick Make the toolpaths too, then click Create.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to see the panels cut out of the board.

steps.title: Assembly View
steps.text: Click Assembly View. The cut panels stand together as the finished box.

steps.title: Check the fit
steps.text: Click Verify Fit to check every joint, and open Cut List for the part sizes. Before the real parts, cut a Test Coupon from the Joint Creator to check the fit.

furniture.title: Design furniture
furniture.blurb: Set sizes on a template; get panels and joints.

steps.title: Open the Assembly View
steps.text: Click Assembly View. Furniture is designed and checked here.

steps.title: Start from a template
steps.text: Click New Furniture to open the Furniture Library, then pick a template you like.

steps.title: Make it your size
steps.text: In the Furniture Designer, type the sizes or drag the sliders. The Assembly View shows the result as you go.

steps.title: Create it
steps.text: Click Create. Zeroed makes the panels on sheets, the joints, the toolpaths and the pieces.

steps.title: See it go together
steps.text: In the Assembly View, drag the Explode slider to pull the pieces apart and see how they fit.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths, pick your post processor and save a file for each sheet.

laser.title: Laser engraving
laser.blurb: Burn text or shapes, with no bit and no depth.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Click Job Setup to tell Zeroed the size and thickness of your material.

steps.title: Material size
steps.text: Type the width, height and thickness of your material, then click OK.

steps.title: Add something to burn
steps.text: Click Create Text to write the words. Vectors you draw or import work the same way.

steps.title: Type the text
steps.text: Click in the view where the text goes, then type the words and pick a font and a height. Click Close when done.

steps.title: Pick what to burn
steps.text: Click the text in the view.

steps.title: Laser Cut & Fill
steps.text: In the Toolpaths panel, click Laser Cut & Fill.

steps.title: Choose the laser
steps.text: Next to Tool, click Select... and pick a laser. Choose Cut On or Hatch Fill, set the Power and Move Speed, then click Calculate.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Click Preview Toolpaths to see the burn before you make it.

steps.title: Save for your machine
steps.text: Click Save Toolpaths and pick a laser post processor. Wear the safety glasses made for your laser, and never leave a running laser alone.
